board_fault.operation: vector load from a4 during kernel vector context restore

root_cause: Ara addrgen retains untranslated virtual addresses in axi_addr_t. The FPGA AXI address width is 48 while architectural virtual addresses are 64 bits. Truncation and subsequent zero extension turn a canonical kernel address into a noncanonical Sv39 address before MMU translation.
historical_masking: The archived MMU canonical check used live request/address inputs instead of the registered request/address. Ara deasserts its MMU request when the response is valid; the old check consequently misses this malformed address in the response cycle. The corrected registered canonical check exposes the latent address-width bug.
simulation_scope: Actual exported addrgen and MMU RTL; controlled valid DTLB hit/PTE; behavioral storage for unexercised TLB/PTW memories. Representative first vector-load request, not full kernel or full SoC simulation.
fix_direction: Separate architectural virtual-address storage/arithmetic from physical AXI address types throughout addrgen, including indexed/strided paths and exception metadata. Narrow only after translation. Keep the corrected MMU canonical check; do not bypass it or blindly reconstruct truncated upper bits.
limits: This identifies the observed init panic; it does not establish that no other Linux or RVV bugs exist, nor validate a corrected bitstream.
